Sophocles, The Trachiniae, translated by Francis Storr.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/sophocles/the-trachiniae/francis-storr

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Sophocles, the author, died 406 BCE.
- Francis Storr, the translator, died 1919.

First publication of the text used: 1913 (SE colophon: 'The Trachiniae was written between 450 and 425 BCE by Sophocles. It was translated from Ancient Greek in 1913 by Francis Storr.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the rights statement quoted below places the text in the United States public domain. The text was first published in 1913, before 1931.
- Country of origin: every person whose words are in the text died in 1925 or earlier, so the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less, whatever its country of first publication.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: the publication year is given in the first-publication line above.
- Wikidata Q7235 (Sophocles), P570 = -0406-00-00; Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophocles.
